newsitem.title: IRAQ: Iraq, Iran exchange remains of soldiers.
newsitem.headline: Iraq, Iran exchange remains of soldiers.

text.p: Iraq and Iran exchanged on Thursday the remains of soldiers missing in action in the 1980- 1988 war between them, the official Iraqi news agency INA said.
The agency said bodies of soldiers from both sides were handed over at Shalamcheh border post east of Basra in southern Iraq.
The agency gave no figures but the Iranian news agency IRNA said on Tuesday that the remains of 40 Iranians and 99 Iraqis would be handed over
INA said a funeral ceremony was held for the Iraqis in Shalamcheh attended by Mayor of Basra and senior army officers.
Iraq and Iran signed an agreement last year on mutual relations and the issue of POWs and remains of soldiers killed during the war, but did not announce the details.
Both have exchanged several hundred POWs and remains of soldiers. In October, Iran freed 150 Iraqi POWs and in August the remains of 400 Iraqis and 65 Iranians were swapped by the two countries.
The missing-in-action and the prisoners of war are among the thorniest problems hindering efforts to improve ties between the former foes.
Iraq denies holding any more Iranians and says more than 20,000 Iraqis are still detained in Iran. Tehran denies the Iraqi claim and says Baghdad is still holding thousands of Iranian POWs.
